ops.title: consent relay leg stays fail-closed on ssh exit 255; probe routes around only on timeout or a status exit

ops.body:
Decision (PR #11, synckit, 2026-10-19; final head 3fab3a6):

- `consent.ProbeRoutesAround` routes around only on `context.DeadlineExceeded` or an `*hostregistry.SSHError` whose ssh exited with a status: `SSHError.Exited` = `*daemonkit.ExitError` with `Exit.Signal == 0` (a remote non-zero exit or ssh's own 255). Anything else fails the request with its cause: a refused spawn, a local signal kill before the deadline (cancelled request, settling scope, outside kill, output cap), or stdin/output failures. A deadline kill still routes around through the timeout branch. Reason: a resident whose fd table passed OPEN_MAX (10240) got EBADF from `posix_spawn_file_actions_adddup2` on every spawn, and the old "any SSHError = offline" rule turned that into a silent routed `unavailable` (cc-sudo exit 104 "no live approver").
- The relay leg's `routesAround` is timeout-only. Its documented exit-255 failover matched `*exec.ExitError`, which `ExecSSH` does not return over a daemonkit runner (verified dead at v0.31.0 and v0.37.0; at v0.25.0 ExecSSH still used os/exec), so production relay 255 had been fatal. Kept fail-closed on purpose: a 255 cannot tell a refused connection from a session dropped after the peer prompted, so failover could prompt a second human after the first answer was lost. Reviving it is a separate, explicit decision.
- Test fakes for ssh failures must wrap `*daemonkit.ExitError`, never `*exec.ExitError`: the exec shape is what let the dead relay check pass tests.
